note: Wave-2 graded items for class 12 Sociology pools (lesy101-107). One-term factual keys and numeric answers; machine-graded.

concepts.title: Sociology and the Need to Unlearn Common Sense

questions.q: Common sense is learned from one's own social group, so it is partial or complete?
The first job of learning sociology is to what common sense?
Turning the outward gaze back and inspecting yourself critically is called what?
The sociologist's first field of observation is what?
Young people form roughly what percent of India's population?
Who you are socially is a set of what on many maps at once?
Which sociologist distinguished personal troubles from social issues: C. Wright Mills or Malthus?
A worry belonging to a single individual is a personal what?
Which basic institutions form the building blocks of Indian society: caste, tribe and family, or banks and malls?
The market entered India as a vehicle of change from which era: colonialism or the Vedic age?
What is the systematic study of population called?
The word demography joins demos with which Greek word for describing?
Malthus said population grows in which progression: geometric or arithmetic?
In which year was Malthus's Essay on population published?
In which stage of demographic transition do death rates fall while birth rates stay high?
India sits in which part of the demographic transition: the middle or the end?
Birth rate counts live births per how many of the population?
Growth rate equals birth rate minus what?

concepts.title: Size and Growth of India's Population

questions.q: Census 2011 counted how many crores of Indians?
In which decade was India's population growth actually negative: 1911-21 or 1961-81?
Which pandemic killed about 5 percent of Indians in 1918?
Population growth jumped to 2.2 percent during which decades: 1961-81 or 1981-2001?
The dependency ratio compares dependents with which age group: 15-64 or 0-6?
India's under-15 share fell from 42 percent in 1971 to what in 2011?
India's sex ratio in 2011 stood at how many females per 1000 males?
The declining sex ratio signals preference for which child: sons or daughters?
About what share of Indians are literate now: two-thirds or one-tenth?
Women trail men in literacy by how many percentage points as of 2011: 16.3 or 2.3?
What share of Indians lived in villages in 2011: 68.8 percent or 12 percent?
Which country was the first to frame a national population policy: India or Britain?

concepts.title: Caste in the Past: Varna and Jati

questions.q: The four-fold all-India division of caste is called what: varna or jati?
The hundreds of regional sub-castes are called what?
Caste membership is fixed by what: birth or wealth?
Caste ranking rests on the opposition of purity and what?
Rules keeping every caste strictly apart express which principle: separation or wholism?
Each caste occupies a fixed rung on a ladder of what?
Under which census officer did the 1901 census record the social rank order of castes: Herbert Risley or Ambedkar?
Which act of 1935 gave legal recognition to scheduled lists of castes?
Colonial counting made caste identities more fluid or more rigid?
The caste census became a ten-yearly exercise from which year: 1881 or 1901?
Raising one's caste status by copying a higher caste's practices is called what?
The numerous intermediate castes with local dominance are called what, in Srinivas's term?
Caste-based parties rose in electoral politics from which decade: the 1980s or the 1950s?
Is mode of livelihood a permanent or an acquired trait in tribal classification?
By language, tribes fall into how many groups: three or thirty?
Which tribe numbers over a million in central India: the Gonds or the Andamanese?
Tribals formed about what percent of India's population at Census 2011: 8.6 or 20?
By the 1970s, standard criteria for the tribe-caste distinction had done what: failed or held?
The two great tribal movement issues are control over land and forests, and what kind of identity?
Tribal identities come from interaction with the mainstream or from primordial traits?
A family of one set of parents and their children is called what: nuclear or extended?
Residence with the husband's family is called what: patrilocal or matrilocal?
Authority resting with the eldest male is called what: patriarchy or matriarchy?

concepts.title: Sociological versus Economic Views of Markets

questions.q: Who wrote the Wealth of Nations: Adam Smith or Karl Marx?
Which metaphor describes self-interested exchanges building an ordered system: the invisible hand or the iron cage?
Sociology holds that markets are embedded in what: culture and social groups, or a vacuum?
The weekly tribal market is called a what: haat or mall?
In the Bastar haat, buyers are mostly adivasis and sellers mainly whom: caste Hindus or officials?
Beyond trade, the haat is a place to meet kin and arrange what?
A bill of exchange honoured within a caste-kin network is called a what?
Which Tamil Nadu community ran a caste-based banking system: the Nakarattars or the Marwaris?
What kept Nakarattar banking sound: a government central bank or shared reputation?
Which Indian industry died under cheap English textiles: handlooms or steel?
Colonialism turned India into a supplier of what and a consumer of finished goods?
Which community rose from migrant traders to industrialists: the Marwaris or the Nakarattars?
In capitalism, workers must sell their what: labour power or land?
Things once outside trade becoming commodities is called what?
Who coined the term status symbol: Weber or Marx?
Name the coaching-based service that has been commodified: education or rainfall?
Since the late 1980s, economies, cultures and politics have been interlinked by what process?
Which Indian traditions are marketed globally as wellness exports: yoga and ayurveda or kabaddi?
When the Pushkar fair becomes a tourism product, what turns into a commodity: a market itself or a mountain?
The government buying farm produce at guaranteed prices is called what: support price or disinvestment?

concepts.title: Social Inequality and Three Forms of Capital

questions.q: Social inequality divides groups or individuals?
Assets and income form which capital, in Bourdieu's terms: economic or cultural?
Networks of contacts and connections form which capital?
Ranking categories of people in a hierarchy is called social what?
Stratification arises once a society produces a what beyond basic needs: surplus or famine?
Stratification persists over generations because position is what: ascribed or achieved?
An opinion formed before evidence is called what?
Fixed, inflexible characterisations of a whole community are called what?
Prejudice put into behaviour is called what?
In 2011-12, what percent of rural Scheduled Tribes lived below the poverty line: 45.3 or 5.3?
Under apartheid, Black workers earned on average what fraction of white earnings: one-fourth or three-fourths?
Seats in legislatures and government jobs set aside for Scheduled Castes and Tribes are called what?
Which article of the Constitution abolishes untouchability: Article 17 or Article 21?
Reservations were extended to the Other Backward Classes from which period: the early 1990s or the 1950s?
Adivasi, coined in the 1930s, means what: original inhabitants or new settlers?
Colonial forests were reserved from the late nineteenth century for what: timber or grazing?
Which tribal region won separate statehood: Jharkhand or Vidarbha?
Who led the fight against sati: Raja Rammohun Roy or Ranade?
Name the matrilineal community of Kerala cited against gender determinism: the Nairs or the Marathas?
Whose 1882 text is an early Indian feminist statement: Tarabai Shinde's or Ranade's?
The differently abled are disabled by impairment and by what else: a society built without them, or fate alone?
Which scholar likens the disabled's invisibility to Ellison's Invisible Man: Anita Ghai or Kalavati?
Is the link between disability and poverty one-directional or two-way?
Diversity stresses difference rather than what: inequality or language?
How many markers does the text list for India's cultural diversity: five or fifty?
The diversity challenge sharpens when identities ride on economic and social what?
Identity resting on birth rather than achievement is called what kind of identity: ascriptive or achieved?
Community identity is felt as total and almost what: inescapable or optional?
Is community identity universal or rare?
A community wanting to share one political collectivity is called a what?
Who defined the state as a body successfully claiming a monopoly of legitimate force: Max Weber or Durkheim?
Nations are communities that have a what of their own: state or flag?
Forcing all citizens toward the dominant culture is called what: assimilation or integration?
Which policy allows minority cultures only in the private sphere: integration or annihilation?
India's alternative accommodates multiple complementary identities and is called a state-what?
Muslims form what percent of India's population per Census 2011: 14.2 or 42?
Whose 1953 fast unto death forced the creation of Andhra: Potti Sriramulu or Jinnah?
Which commission reorganised states on a linguistic basis in 1956: the States Reorganisation Commission or the Finance Commission?
Accommodation of regional diversity runs through what arrangement: federalism or unitary rule?
In sociology, minority implies small numbers plus what: relative disadvantage or height?
Left-handed people are not a minority because they lack what: group solidarity forged by prejudice, or numbers?
Which two articles shield religious and cultural minorities: Articles 29 and 30, or 14 and 15?
Aggressive political chauvinism built on religious identity is called what?
Indian secularism means equal respect for all religions or strict separation of religion and state?
Communalism is an ideology or a faith?
The arena beyond family, state and market where citizens form voluntary associations is called what?
Under the right to information rules, replies are due within how many days: thirty or three hundred?
Which body of the state is listed alongside legislature and judiciary: the bureaucracy or a trade union?

concepts.title: Choosing a Research Question and Method

questions.q: Before choosing a method, a broad topic must be narrowed into one specific what?
What must match before a study begins: question and method, or mood and method?
Practical constraints on method choice include time, people, materials and what else?
A survey asks a large number of people the same what of questions: fixed set or changing set?
An interview is always conducted in what way: in person or by post?
Observation requires watching and recording how: systematically or casually?
A group never seen entering a public space shows the value of what method?
Observation must log events fairly before any what?
Studying today's media by survey and past media by archives combines methods by doing what: pairing them or dropping one?
Combining methods covers each method's what: blind side or strong side?
Is combining methods highly recommended or forbidden?
Behaviour and etiquette at a bus station suit which method: observation or a census?
Opinions on household appliances suit which method: a survey or a coin toss?
Which theme tracks hopes across age groups: changing aspirations or the biography of a commodity?
